issues.description: Fix only normalizes ClassName; ID, attribute, type, and pseudo selectors with escapes will still false-negative
issues.detail: CSS escapes are legal in identifiers everywhere: `#u-m\+` vs `#u-m\00002b`, `[data-x=\+]` vs `[data-x=\00002b]`, type selectors like `\+foo`, pseudo-class arguments, etc. The data structure here is `node.value` on any selector-parser node that carries an identifier; the algorithm is the same trick (`node.value = node.value`). Gating on `parser.isClassName` solves one shape of the data and leaves the rest broken. Either widen to every node kind that exposes a value getter/setter, or document explicitly why ClassName is the only case worth fixing.

issues.description: Two walks now run per node where one would do
issues.detail: `normalizeSelector` already walks the tree once for whitespace/comments. The new code adds `normalizeNodeEscaping` to the same walk plus a separate up-front call for the root. That is fine, but the pattern would be cleaner as a single normalize function applied uniformly to root and descendants. n is small so it does not matter for speed; it matters for code shape. The data is a tree of nodes; the algorithm is `for each node, normalize`. Make that the obvious thing.

issues.description: `node.value = node.value` with eslint-disable depends on undocumented library behavior
issues.detail: The fix is clever: it abuses a getter/setter side effect in postcss-selector-parser to re-normalize escaping. It works, but it is load-bearing cleverness that future maintainers will read as a no-op and delete. The comment is good; consider also wrapping in a tiny named helper like `renormalizeEscaping(node)` so the call site reads as intent rather than as a self-assignment lint-bypass. Prefer a documented API if one exists.

issues.description: `raws.value` early-return is a perf hack reaching past the type boundary
issues.detail: The `@ts-expect-error` plus `node.raws?.value` check is justified as a perf optimization, but rule 1 of the rules of programming applies: do not put in a speed hack until you have proven the bottleneck. Selector normalization runs on small n. Either measure and keep the gate with a comment citing the measurement, or drop the gate and let the setter run unconditionally. As written it is type-unsafe optimization without a number behind it.

issues.description: Test coverage matches the implementation scope, not the bug class
issues.detail: Tests cover class selectors with hex-vs-character and short-vs-long hex escapes. They do not cover ID selectors, attribute values, type selectors, or pseudo-class arguments with escapes. If the intent is `no-duplicate-selectors handles escape equivalence`, the test list should reflect that and either pass for all node kinds or have explicit `accept` cases documenting the known gaps.

review.summary: The fix picks the right tool — let the parser's own getter/setter normalize escaping rather than reinventing CSS escape parsing. That is good data-structure thinking: do not duplicate work the library already does. The problem is scope. The bug class is "equivalent escape sequences should compare equal," and the data shape (a value field on selector-parser nodes) is the same across ClassName, IdSelector, Attribute, Tag, and Pseudo. Gating on isClassName leaves the algorithm fighting a subset of the data. Decision: COULD-BE-A-FILTER and slightly TOO-CLEVER — widen the normalization to every node kind that carries an escapable value, fold the two walks into one uniform pass, and either justify the raws.value gate with a measurement or drop it.
